clue.text: Ruin unloved folk instrument with interminable rock guitar

indicators.note: love in crossword scoring is zero, O, so unloved means that O-shaped letter is dropped

parts.note: the banjo is a stringed folk instrument

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: axe is rock musicians' slang for a guitar

explanation.surface: A folk musician's banjo, drowned out by an endless electric guitar solo, is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unloved' drops O from BANJO; 'interminable' cuts the E from AXE, US-spelt AX.
explanation.definitionFit: Banjax is Irish-origin slang meaning to wreck or break something completely.

clue.text: An ancient more primitive love affair

parts.note: the indefinite article
mo is an archaic word for more
ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original

explanation.surface: A puzzled comment that an old, cruder romance is somehow more primitive.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is an old dialect form of 'more'; UR is the German-derived prefix seen in 'ur-text'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a French-borrowed word for a romance, especially an illicit or secret one.

clue.text: Scaremonger to skip eating refined butter

indicators.note: eating means the dance word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to jig is to skip or dance about

indicators.note: refined here means processed and reworked, so the letters of butter are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who spreads fear avoids food made with clarified butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined butter' looks like ghee but is an anagram; 'to skip' is a verb meaning to dance, not to miss out.
explanation.definitionFit: A jitterbug is a nervous person, and by extension one who spreads alarm.

clue.text: Looked into beginning to date after kiss on new year

indicators.note: after places the first letter of date at the end, behind the rest

parts.note: X is the conventional sign for a kiss

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of year
beginning to picks only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A romantic check on a date after a New Year's kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns YEAR into RAYE; 'beginning to' gives D from date.
explanation.definitionFit: To X-ray something is to examine its inside with radiation, so looked into literally.

clue.text: Discover pencil pusher giving away American code

indicators.note: dis-cover read as removing the cover, the outer letters of pencil
giving away says the following letters are dropped from pusher

explanation.surface: An office worker discovers an American secret code and gives it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discover' strips pencil to ENCI; 'giving away' takes US from PUSHER to leave PHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To encipher is to put a message into code, so the verb sense of code.

clue.text: Competition adapted garden gnome's cap, making end of pompom round

indicators.note: adapted means the letters are altered into a new order
the last letter of pompom, M, is made round, that is turned into the round letter O

explanation.surface: A garden gnome's hat is adapted so its pompom ends up round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making end of pompom round' swaps the M of GARDEN GNOMES CAP for O; 'adapted' then rearranges the fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-and-spoon race is a school sports-day contest, carrying an egg balanced on a spoon.

clue.text: Rope lassoing display of cowboy skill, mostly getting rusty

indicators.note: lassoing means roping something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cord is a thin rope

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a rodeo is a show of cowboy riding and roping

explanation.surface: A cowboy's rope at a rodeo, mostly getting rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link: the definition is 'rusty' alone, though 'mostly' sits next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Corroded metal has been eaten away by rust or chemicals, a close synonym of rusty.

clue.text: Detective essentially quizzing a Hawaiian, perhaps

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of the word, its two central letters

explanation.surface: A detective, at heart, interrogating a man from Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the central ZZ of quizzing. 'perhaps' marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian is a pizza topped with ham and pineapple, one example of the dish.

clue.text: Exciting novel out about international development

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the other letter
exciting means stirring up, so the letters of novel out are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrilling novel about global development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exciting' rearranges NOVEL OUT; 'about' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual development, whether of species or of ideas.

clue.text: Hide point of heroin needle — it can support one's habit

parts.note: a coat is an animal's hide or pelt

indicators.note: the point is the tip, the first letter of heroin

parts.note: needle as a noun means irritation or anger

explanation.surface: A drug user hides the tip of a heroin needle, feeding their habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' reads as addiction but means clothing, like a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat hanger holds up a garment, and a habit is a garment, as worn by monks.

clue.text: Merseyside's first safari park starting to change focus rapidly

indicators.note: starting puts the park word at the beginning, ahead of the letter

parts.note: a safari park is a kind of zoo

indicators.note: first picks only the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Merseyside's first safari park is starting to change its focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' places ZOO first, before M from 'Merseyside's first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera zooms when its lens shifts quickly between wide and close-up views.

clue.text: Seabird circling key tropical plant

indicators.note: circling means the bird goes round the other piece

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a key, or cay, is a low island or reef

explanation.surface: A seabird wheels round a tropical island covered with plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is not a lock or piano key here but a low island, a reef.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree ferns are tall ferns with trunks, growing in tropical and subtropical forests.

clue.text: Initially old puzzles appear quite unusual, even cryptic

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Old puzzles seem quite odd, even cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means hard to understand, obscure, the same sense as cryptic.

clue.text: Book on cycling was clean

indicators.note: on places the book letter after the other piece in an across answer
cycling means the letters rotate round, the last moving to the front

explanation.surface: A book about cycling was clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the S of WAS to the front, giving SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: To swab is to wipe or mop something clean, as sailors swab a deck.

clue.text: Horny material in W. H. Auden's introduction upset Nobel committee ultimately

parts.note: the poet's initials, taken as written

indicators.note: introduction means the opening letter of the word
upset means knocked over, so the letters of Nobel are jumbled
ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The poet W. H. Auden's introduction upsets the Nobel prize committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOBEL into LEBON.
explanation.definitionFit: Whalebone is baleen, the keratin plates in whales' mouths, so a horny substance.

clue.text: Don't change this without set-back during work — hurry

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the instruction goes round the rest

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to leave text unchanged

indicators.note: set back means turned round, so the two short words read in reverse

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the meantime'
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Instructions to an editor: don't change this, avoid setbacks at work, and hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' gives PONI. 'without' is not 'lacking' here but its old sense of outside, so the proofreader's mark wraps round the reversed pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom for hurry up, from pressing the accelerator.

clue.text: Firm returning some gadget a nit's bought

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A firm, stubborn idiot sticks to a gadget he bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of unyielding, which is what an obstinate person is.

clue.text: George V and Edward VIII and maybe, Prince Michael of Kent

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is George V's royal cipher
taken as written
Edward VIII was George V's son, so his relation to the king gives son

explanation.surface: A list of British royals across three generations.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Michael of Kent is a grandson of George V; 'maybe' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Michael of Kent is one example of a grandson, being George V's son's son.

clue.text: Kylie originally sang all but the opening — a flipping gold disc follows for this iconic Australian

indicators.note: follows means the rest comes after what has gone before
originally points to the first letter of Kylie
all but the opening means the word without its first letter
flipping means turning over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: Kylie Minogue sings, and a gold disc follows for the Australian pop icon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but the opening' cuts SANG to ANG; 'flipping' turns OR to RO. Kylie Minogue is an Australian pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: The kangaroo is the animal most identified with Australia, on its coat of arms.

clue.text: Bad European function

parts.note: sin as a word for wrongdoing, what is bad

explanation.surface: A wicked European official.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is a trigonometric function, the ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse.

clue.text: In retirement, occasionally, spouse insults garage job

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing, going back, so the letters read in reverse
occasionally means every other letter only

explanation.surface: In retirement, a husband or wife now and then insults the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes PUENUT from spouse insults; 'In retirement' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune-up is a service adjusting a car's engine, routine work at a garage.

clue.text: You and I take no time with new exhaust

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: no means without, so the following letter is dropped

explanation.surface: We take no time fitting a new exhaust pipe to the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops T from TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust is to tire or deplete, which weakens someone.

clue.text: Perhaps automatic starter sounded buff

indicators.note: sounded means spoken, so the answer sounds like the words

parts.note: an automatic is one kind of car; a key is what starts a car

explanation.surface: An automatic starter motor, perhaps, sounds good to a car buff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, car key sounds like khaki.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff and khaki are both dull yellowish-brown colours.

clue.text: One man cuts film out — losing all extreme characters — and finally appreciates Finding Nemo's craft

indicators.note: each word loses its outside letters, leaving only the inner ones
finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A film editor cuts extremes from a film, and finally appreciates Finding Nemo.
explanation.walkthrough: N, A, UT, IL, U are the insides of the five words. Not Pixar's fish: Captain Nemo's submarine in Jules Verne.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautilus is the submarine commanded by Captain Nemo in Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

clue.text: Higher direct debit for very quiet milk supplier

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another

parts.note: upper means higher
pp, pianissimo, is very quiet in music
DD is the banking abbreviation for direct debit

explanation.surface: A higher direct debit to pay for a very quiet milk delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: DD replaces the PP in UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An udder is the cow's gland that supplies its milk.

clue.text: Seat getting lower at one end according to the notes

parts.note: so is a note in tonic sol-fa
fa, the next note below so in tonic sol-fa, put at the end

explanation.surface: A seat that sags lower at one end, according to the notes.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa (do, re, mi, fa, so...), FA is one step below SO, so the lower of the pair comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: Crook runs away — suspect Den has to agree a deal

indicators.note: away means the letter is gone from the word

parts.note: a shark is a swindler, a crook
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook runs off, while a suspect called Den has to agree to a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' takes R from SHARK; 'suspect' rearranges DEN HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking hands is the gesture that seals an agreement.

clue.text: Confrontation both sides of divorce intended

indicators.note: both sides means the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiance

explanation.surface: Both partners in a divorce intended to confront each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a standing up to someone.

clue.text: Dig entertaining love film — it's lyrical

indicators.note: entertaining means holding inside, so the other letters go in

parts.note: to pry is to dig into or poke about
love is zero, O, in tennis scoring
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Someone digs a love film and says it's lyrical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' is slang for like but means pry.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is verse, the form of writing that lyrical describes.
